nodes.long_description:
Vista Pictures VR is a viewer built for the way you actually use a headset.

SEE EVERYTHING YOU OWN
Photos, 3D models, 360 HDRI environments and material textures, all in one browser. Images in JPEG, PNG, WebP, HEIF and more. Models in GLB, glTF, STL, OBJ, PLY and 3MF, including the files that come out of a slicer. HDRI skies in Radiance and OpenEXR, up to 16K.

TURN ANY PHOTO INTO 3D
Open a flat photo and see it in real stereo depth, with a slider for how far it stands out. The depth model runs on the headset itself — nothing is uploaded — and each result is kept, so the second look is instant. Your own photos, finally worth putting a headset on for.

STEP INSIDE
Open anything in a full immersive space. Stand inside a 360 sky, orbit a model at any scale, and see it lit by the environment around it. Key light, ambient, reflections and shadows on real sliders. Nine colour grades. Dress a model in glass, metal, marble or wood. Passthrough on an opacity slider, so your room shows through whatever you are viewing.

BRING IN MORE
Search Poly Haven from inside the app and download skies, models and textures at the resolution you choose. Everything there is free and public domain.

REACH YOUR FILES
Headset storage, USB drives, SMB and network shares, Dropbox, Google Drive and OneDrive. Thumbnails are cached in the background, so scrolling stays smooth even through folders of 8K skies.

Ships with sample images, so there is something to look at from the very first launch.
nodes.short_description: Vista Pictures VR turns your Quest into a proper viewer for everything visual you own. View photos at full resolution, walk around 3D models, and stand inside 360 HDRI skies. Open files from headset storage, a network share or your cloud drive. Thumbnails load instantly and models appear the moment they are read. Light, grade and inspect anything in an immersive space, then search Poly Haven for free CC0 skies, models and textures without ever taking the headset off.

nodes.change_log:
1.0.0 (9) — fixes the unresponsive state (black screen when going back)

Also:
- Poly Haven downloads default to 8K for skies and 2K for textures and models instead of 'Max'.
- Storage permission is re-checked on resume
- Bitmap and panorama ceilings are read from the device: Quest 2 (6 GB) gets 8K skies, 4096
  pictures, 2048 textures; Quest 3 / 3S / Pro (8 GB) keep 16K, 8192, 4096.
- Thumbnail cache is bounded with least-recently-used eviction; it previously grew without
  limit on a large library.

1.0.0 (6) — completes the fix for the ANRs reported on Textures and Images.

The crash panel named two causes, PatternNative.compileImpl and MatcherNative.matchesImpl.
Both are regular expressions on the main thread, and there were exactly two places doing that.

1. The texture classifier compiled a regex for every token of every file name, on every batch
   of scan results, on the main thread — and it runs for the Images and Textures categories
   and for no others, which is why those two tabs were the ones that stopped responding. The
   pattern is now compiled once, and it is tried last of three tests, so for most tokens no
   matcher is created at all. The classification also moved off the main thread, and partial
   scan results are delivered on a 400 ms clock instead of every 20 files, which removes work
   that grew with the square of the library.

2. The syntax highlighter built 76 Regex objects on every recomposition of the text editor —
   every keystroke, every scroll — and ran them all over the whole document. Patterns are now
   compiled once and kept, and files over 128 KB are shown without colouring.

Also in this build:
- Applying a texture or opening a picture no longer decodes at unbounded size. An 8K material
  map is 268 MB decoded before GL takes its own copy; both are now bounded, and the pixel copy
  handed to the renderer runs on a worker rather than the main thread.
- Memory ceilings are read from the device: Quest 2 (6 GB) gets 8K skies, 4096 pictures and
  2048 textures; Quest 3 / 3S / Pro (8 GB) keep 16K, 8192 and 4096. Nothing visible is lost —
  8K equirect already exceeds what these panels resolve.
- The thumbnail cache is bounded with least-recently-used eviction; it previously grew without
  limit on a large library.
- Category scans skip Android/, stop when the user leaves the tab, and refuse a model too
  large to read rather than dying without a message.
- Uncaught exceptions are recorded to logcat and to a file, so a fault in the field can be
  diagnosed rather than guessed at.

1.0.0 (5) — fixes for the crash reported on Textures and Images.

Two faults were found, both landing on exactly those two tabs.

1. Opening Images or Textures did work proportional to the SQUARE of the library. The scan
   handed partial results to the UI every 20 files, and for those two categories the UI then
   re-sorted and re-classified everything found so far on the main thread. On a library of a
   few thousand pictures that is tens of seconds of a frozen main thread — the app stops
   submitting frames and is taken away, which is what a crash looks like from outside.
   Partial results are now delivered on a 400 ms clock, and the classification runs on a
   worker. The classifier itself was also made linear (4x faster on its own).

2. Applying a texture or opening a picture decoded the file at whatever size it happened to
   be, with no ceiling. An 8K material map — the standard size in texture libraries — is
   268 MB decoded, and GL then takes its own copy with a mip chain. Both are now bounded, and
   the pixel copy handed to the renderer no longer runs on the main thread.

Also in this build:
- Memory ceilings are read from the device, so Quest 2 (6 GB) gets 8K skies, 4096 pictures and
  2048 textures while Quest 3 / 3S / Pro (8 GB) keep 16K, 8192 and 4096. Nothing visible is
  lost: 8K equirect already exceeds what these panels resolve.
- The thumbnail cache is bounded with least-recently-used eviction; it previously grew without
  limit on a large library.
- Category scans skip Android/, stop when the user leaves the tab, and refuse a model too
  large to read rather than dying without a message.
- Uncaught exceptions are now recorded to logcat and to a file, so a fault in the field can be
  diagnosed rather than guessed at.

1.0.0 (4) — first alpha.

Viewer for photos, 3D models, 360 HDRI environments and material textures.
- Immersive view for every media type, with lighting, colour grades and passthrough
- 2D to 3D depth conversion, running on the headset
- Poly Haven search and download built in, downloads continue with the headset off
- Sources: headset storage, USB, SMB/FTP/SFTP/WebDAV, Dropbox, Google Drive, OneDrive
- Ships with 42 sample images

Since build 3: POST_NOTIFICATIONS removed. It was never requested at runtime, so on
targetSdk 34 it was never granted and enabled nothing; downloads and file operations are
unaffected.

1.0.0 (3) — first alpha.

Viewer for photos, 3D models, 360 HDRI environments and material textures.
- Immersive view for every media type, with lighting, colour grades and passthrough
- 2D to 3D depth conversion, running on the headset
- Poly Haven search and download built in, downloads continue with the headset off
- Sources: headset storage, USB, SMB/FTP/SFTP/WebDAV, Dropbox, Google Drive, OneDrive
- Ships with 42 sample images

Since build 2: HDRI textures upload across frames instead of one long stall, so loading a
sky no longer drops frames or lets the system environment show through.
